g1|variants|dsd.summary: Direct Store Delivery in SAP S/4HANA combines order execution, van sales, and pre-sales route accounting with OTC billing and inventory. The variants differ by whether the driver performs pre-sales order collection, van sales with immediate physical delivery and billing, or direct store check-in/check-out reconciliation.

variants.name: Van Sales (Cash Sale) with On-Board Billing
variants.when_used: Driver sells stock directly from the vehicle, delivers immediately, and prints the invoice on-site.
variants.key_config: Assign DSD tour type to sales area, configure cash sale document type BV, and enable mobile billing integration.

variants.name: Pre-Sales Order Collection
variants.when_used: Sales representative visits customers to record orders which are later fulfilled via standard delivery and billing.
variants.key_config: Configure visit control, customer hierarchy for DSD, and integration with sales order creation via handheld devices.

variants.name: Check-In / Check-Out Reconciliation
variants.when_used: Reconciliation of physical stock and cash loaded onto the truck at departure and returned after the tour.
variants.key_config: Set up DSD freight document types, driver settlement profiles, and discrepancy processing rules for cash/stock.

variants.name: Direct Delivery with Customer Return Processing
variants.when_used: Driver picks up damaged goods or customer returns during the route and posts them back into inventory upon settlement.
variants.key_config: Configure return delivery types, inspection codes, and credit memo request generation during tour settlement.

g1|core|dsd|van sales (cash sale) with o.title: Direct Store Delivery (DSD) -- Van Sales (Cash Sale) with On-Board Billing
g1|core|dsd|van sales (cash sale) with o.story: Imagine a delivery truck filled with products that acts as a mobile grocery store making unexpected stops at local shops. In SAP S/4HANA, this Van Sales process uses a Cash Sale order type BV, generates a delivery BV, issues goods with movement type 651, and prints an invoice directly from the handheld device using billing type IV. When the driver returns to the depot, the system reconciles the cash collected against the printed on-board invoices.
g1|core|dsd|van sales (cash sale) with o.why_business_needs_it: Consumer goods companies require Van Sales with on-board billing to service small, cash-and-carry retail outlets where orders, deliveries, and payments must happen instantaneously in a single visit. It eliminates delayed back-office billing cycles and instantly updates mobile inventory and cash ledgers.

g1|core|dsd|pre-sales order collection.title: Direct Store Delivery (DSD) Pre-Sales Order Collection
g1|core|dsd|pre-sales order collection.story: Just like a friendly neighborhood ice cream truck driver who writes down everyone's favorite flavors on a notepad before scooping them out of the big freezer, our sales representatives visit stores to capture customer orders before sending them over to the warehouse for delivery. Technically, this process leverages Direct Store Delivery (DSD) Pre-Sales integration within SAP S/4HANA Order-to-Cash, capturing orders in the field, determining route schedules and visit lists, and handing off the resulting standard sales orders (OR) for subsequent outbound delivery (LF) and billing (F2) execution.
g1|core|dsd|pre-sales order collection.why_business_needs_it: This process enables field sales representatives to systematically capture customer demand during route visits, feeding directly into efficient warehouse picking, packing, and transportation planning. It optimizes route execution and ensures seamless billing and revenue recognition upon goods issue (movement type 601).

modules.role: Manages pre-sales orders, route accounting, visit lists, pricing, outbound deliveries, and billing.
modules.hands_off_to: LE-WM / EWM for picking, packing, and outbound delivery execution based on movement type 601.

modules.role: Processes outbound delivery documents (LF) and posts goods issue.
modules.hands_off_to: FI-AR for customer invoice posting and revenue recognition.

modules.role: Receives billing data from billing type F2 to post open items and process customer payments.

g1|core|dsd|check-in / check-out reconci.title: Direct Store Delivery Check-In / Check-Out Reconciliation
g1|core|dsd|check-in / check-out reconci.story: Imagine a delivery driver filling up a magic truck with toys, driving to shops, selling some, and then bringing back the leftover toys and money to count everything together. Technically, the Direct Store Delivery (DSD) Check-In / Check-Out Reconciliation process manages the physical inventory and financial settlement of a tour driver returning from a route, reconciling loaded stock, sales, returns, and cash collections against the outbound delivery and billing documents.
g1|core|dsd|check-in / check-out reconci.why_business_needs_it: It ensures complete financial and inventory accuracy by matching physical goods returned from a vehicle against system deliveries and billing documents. Without it, companies suffer from inventory shrinkage, unaccounted cash differences, and unresolved billing discrepancies.

g1|core|dsd|direct delivery with custome.title: Direct Delivery with Customer Return Processing
g1|core|dsd|direct delivery with custome.story: Imagine a delivery driver picking up unwanted items directly from a store and bringing them back while updating the system on the spot. Precise definition: This Direct Store Delivery (DSD) return scenario executes customer returns initiated during field visits, creating a Return Order (RE) in SAP S/4HANA Sales, generating a subsequent Returns Delivery (LR), posting goods receipt via movement type 651, and issuing a Credit Memo (G2) in Sales and Distribution (SD) for financial settlement.
g1|core|dsd|direct delivery with custome.why_business_needs_it: It streamlines field-based merchandise returns by linking mobile route settlement directly to customer credit memo generation. This ensures real-time inventory visibility for returned stock and accurate financial accounting without manual back-office re-entry.

g1|panel|dsd.otc_impact: Direct Store Delivery (DSD) sits at the intersection of mobile field execution, inventory management, and Order-to-Cash, orchestrating complex van sales, pre-sales, and reconciliation cycles. It transforms standard OTC operations by moving order creation, delivery fulfillment, on-board billing, and cash collection from the static back-office to mobile devices loaded onto delivery trucks. This integration ensures seamless hand-offs from sales orders to outbound deliveries, driver loading, settlement, and final invoice generation or cash posting, directly impacting Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) and order-to-cash velocity.

panel_qa.question: How does DSD van sales handle immediate inventory decrement and on-board billing without disrupting standard S/4HANA stock and accounting ledgers?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Direct Store Delivery van sales execute physical delivery and billing simultaneously in the field via mobile devices integrated with SAP DSD backend functions. SAP is configured this way to bridge disconnected remote transactions with core financials by utilizing specialized movement types and interim truck stock storage locations. Key configuration involves assigning specific sales document types (e.g., cash sales type BV) linked to immediate delivery-related billing and cash sales billing types (CB) in transaction VOV8. The leadership value is instantaneous revenue recognition and precise truck inventory visibility, eliminating reconciliation lag and reducing working capital requirements. Next steps involve monitoring settlement IDoc processing and cash drawer balancing jobs in backend settlement cockpit /DSD/CH_SETTL. Trap: Treating van sales like a standard warehouse delivery order without accounting for mobile stock transfers.
panel_qa.trap: Treating van sales like a standard warehouse delivery order without accounting for mobile stock transfers.

panel_qa.question: What are the financial risks and control mechanisms during the DSD check-in and check-out reconciliation process?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Check-In and Check-Out reconciliation governs the physical inventory loaded onto delivery trucks, returned goods, and collected cash or checks returned by drivers. SAP enforces this via the DSD Tour Data Medium and Settlement Cockpit to reconcile loaded quantities against sold quantities and cash received. Key configuration includes defining tour control parameters, settlement profiles, and difference reason codes in transaction /DSD/VC_ST_PROF to route variances to specific general ledger clearing accounts. The leadership value is airtight financial control over field assets and cash collection, mitigating shrinkage and unapplied cash risks. Next steps involve auditing daily settlement logs and ensuring proper segregation of duties between drivers and cashiers. Trap: Allowing drivers to settle cash without automated matching against generated billing documents.
panel_qa.trap: Allowing drivers to settle cash without automated matching against generated billing documents.

panel_qa.question: How do we manage pre-sales order collection workflows where mobile sales reps capture orders that must convert into centralized deliveries?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Pre-sales order collection allows field representatives to record customer orders on mobile devices for subsequent fulfillment from a distribution center rather than the truck stock. SAP is configured this way to separate order capture from physical delivery execution while maintaining customer-specific pricing and credit limits. Key configuration involves inbound IDoc processing using message type ORDERS for sales order creation (e.g., standard order type OR) via process code ORDR. The leadership value is expanded sales reach with centralized inventory control and streamlined order processing pipelines. Next steps include tuning background jobs for batch delivery creation (VL10G) and output determination for picking. Trap: Manually re-entering mobile pre-sales orders into the SAP GUI.
panel_qa.trap: Manually re-entering mobile pre-sales orders into the SAP GUI.

panel_qa.question: How does DSD handle customer returns processed directly at the store during delivery or van sales?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Direct delivery with customer return processing enables drivers to accept damaged or unsold goods on-site and issue immediate credit memos or adjusted invoices. SAP integrates this by creating return delivery documents referencing the original invoice or sales order, followed by inspection and stock placement back into truck or warehouse return locations. Key configuration requires return order types (e.g., RE) with item categories (e.g., REN) set for returns and credit memo request generation in transaction VOV7. The leadership value is enhanced customer satisfaction through rapid dispute resolution and accurate inventory valuation for damaged stock. Next steps involve setting up quality inspection codes and automatic credit memo posting workflows. Trap: Processing returns as standard goods receipts without generating a corresponding return order and credit document.
panel_qa.trap: Processing returns as standard goods receipts without generating a corresponding return order and credit document.

panel_qa.question: What is the architectural roadmap for DSD in S/4HANA Private Cloud, and how does it integrate with mobile client solutions?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: DSD in S/4HANA Private Edition relies on backend Direct Store Delivery components communicating with mobile apps via SAP BTP or middleware adapters using OData services and IDocs. SAP maintains this architecture to support high-volume transaction processing while transitioning away from legacy SAP GUI transactions toward Fiori-enabled settlement tools. Key configuration centers on activating OData services for DSD tour management and configuring RFC destinations for mobile data exchange. The leadership value is a future-proof, scalable field execution platform with reduced total cost of ownership and improved system responsiveness. Next steps include migrating legacy RF/mobile transactions to standard SAP Fiori apps for tour dispatching and settlement. Trap: Assuming classic Direct Store Delivery ABAP stack works out-of-the-box in modern S/4HANA Cloud without activation and extension adjustments.
panel_qa.trap: Assuming classic Direct Store Delivery ABAP stack works out-of-the-box in modern S/4HANA Cloud without activation and adjustment.

panel_qa.question: How do we configure credit limit checks for van sales where orders and deliveries occur simultaneously in the field?
panel_qa.how_to_answer: Van sales require synchronous credit checks because the delivery and billing occur offline or in real-time before back-office approval can be secured. SAP handles this by performing static or dynamic credit checks at the sales document creation stage on the mobile device or upon backend IDoc import prior to billing release. Key configuration involves assigning automatic credit control areas to the sales area and setting up check rules in transaction OVA8. The leadership value is proactive risk mitigation against bad debt from unverified cash or credit customers on delivery routes. Next steps include configuring blocked order release workflows for credit managers using transaction VKM1. Trap: Disabling credit checks entirely for van sales to avoid field transaction delays.
panel_qa.trap: Disabling credit checks entirely for van sales to avoid field transaction delays.

doc_flow.what: Sales document type RE records customer returns originating from DSD route execution or customer service requests.
Delivery type LR governs the inbound physical movement and logistics processing of returned goods.
Material document posts returned physical inventory into restricted or returns stock using movement type 651.
Billing type G2 settles the customer account by issuing a credit memo referencing the return delivery.
